sources.title: Existence of a phase-transition in a one-dimensional Ising ferromagnet
sources.author: F. J. Dyson
sources.description: The one-dimensional Ising model with pair couplings decaying as a power: a transition exists for decay exponent between one and two. Introduces the hierarchical approximation that later carries the renormalisation group exactly.

sources.title: Investigation of the critical point in models of the type of Dyson's hierarchical models
sources.author: P. M. Bleher and Ya. G. Sinai
sources.description: The renormalisation transformation of the hierarchical model as a nonlinear map on probability measures, with the critical point identified as the boundary between two domains of attraction.

sources.title: Critical indices for Dyson's asymptotically-hierarchical models
sources.author: P. M. Bleher and Ya. G. Sinai
sources.description: Critical indices of the hierarchical model from the spectrum of the linearised renormalisation map, including the non-Gaussian fixed point and the classical region.

sources.title: A rigorous block spin approach to massless lattice theories
sources.author: K. Gawedzki and A. Kupiainen
sources.description: A convergent block-spin expansion for lattice field theories, with the hierarchical model as the worked example and as the approximation justifying the Euclidean expansion.

sources.title: Non-Gaussian fixed points of the block spin transformation. Hierarchical model approximation
sources.author: K. Gawedzki and A. Kupiainen
sources.description: Existence and local analysis of the nontrivial fixed points of the hierarchical renormalisation map: the epsilon expansion, the unstable manifold, and its normal form.

sources.title: Non-Gaussian scaling limits. Hierarchical model approximation
sources.author: K. Gawedzki and A. Kupiainen
sources.description: Scaling limits of the hierarchical model governed by the nontrivial fixed point, and the renormalisation-group flow of the relevant direction around it.

sources.title: Critical exponents for long-range interactions
sources.author: M. Aizenman and R. Fernandez
sources.description: Classical values of the long-range Ising exponents in the mean-field region, with the marginal case included.

sources.title: Critical exponents for long-range interactions
sources.author: M. E. Fisher, S.-k. Ma and B. G. Nickel
sources.description: The classical long-range exponent values as functions of the decay exponent, and the upper critical decay rate at which they cease to hold.

sources.title: Long-range percolation on the hierarchical lattice
sources.author: V. Koval, R. Meester and P. Trapman
sources.description: The phase transition of long-range percolation on the hierarchical lattice: a finite critical intensity exactly when the kernel exponent is below the dimension, and no infinite cluster at criticality.

sources.title: The critical two-point function for long-range percolation on the hierarchical lattice
sources.author: T. Hutchcroft
sources.description: Critical connection probabilities on the hierarchical lattice of order the distance to the power minus the dimension minus the kernel exponent, the volume exponent obstruction above the triangle threshold, and mean-field consequences below it.

sources.title: Correlations in Ising ferromagnets
sources.author: R. B. Griffiths
sources.description: The correlation inequalities for ferromagnetic Ising systems: monotonicity in the couplings and fields, and the positivity of the correlation of two disjoint sets of spins.

sources.title: Regularity properties and pathologies of position-space renormalization-group transformations: scope and limitations of Gibbsian theory
sources.author: A. C. D. van Enter, R. Fernandez and A. D. Sokal
sources.description: Block-spin transformations of Gibbs measures need not be Gibbs measures, so position-space decimation does not preserve a space of interactions in general.

sources.title: Mean-field behavior for long- and finite range Ising model, percolation and self-avoiding walk
sources.author: M. Heydenreich, R. van der Hofstad and A. Sakai
sources.description: Lace-expansion proof of mean-field behaviour for long-range models, with the dimension thresholds in terms of the decay exponent.

sources.title: Critical (Phi^4) in three dimensions
sources.author: D. C. Brydges, P. K. Mitter and B. Scoppola
sources.description: A renormalisation-group trajectory for a critical Euclidean field theory, the argument being organised by the hierarchical analysis of the same map.

sources.title: Introduction to a Renormalisation Group Method
sources.author: R. Bauerschmidt, D. C. Brydges and G. Slade
sources.description: Self-contained development of the renormalisation group for lattice field theory, beginning from the hierarchical model as the model in which the map is a one-variable recursion.

sources.title: Renormalization of Dyson's hierarchical vector valued φ⁴ model at low temperatures
sources.author: P. M. Bleher and P. Major
sources.description: The renormalisation of the vector-valued hierarchical φ⁴ model in its low-temperature phase, where the continuous symmetry leaves a Goldstone direction.

sources.title: Critical phenomena and universal exponents in statistical physics. On Dyson's hierarchical model
sources.author: P. M. Bleher and P. Major
sources.description: A survey of the hierarchical model as a problem about the limit distribution of partial sums of strongly dependent variables: critical behaviour and exponents with sketches of proofs, the vector case, and conjectures.

sources.title: A Thouless-like effect in the Dyson hierarchical model with continuous symmetry
sources.author: P. M. Bleher and P. Major
sources.description: Dyson's conjecture for the r-component hierarchical model: a phase transition exactly when the interaction sequence fails to be summable, no Thouless effect in the spontaneous magnetisation, and a uniform limit law on the sphere for the normalised average spin at criticality.

sources.title: Hierarchical models and renormalisation group. Critical phenomena in the Dyson hierarchical model and renormalisation group
sources.author: P. M. Bleher
sources.description: A historical account of the Moscow seminar on mathematical statistical physics and of the renormalisation group for Dyson's hierarchical model.

sources.title: Theory of Phase Transitions: Rigorous Results
sources.author: Ya. G. Sinai
sources.description: The rigorous theory of phase transitions and limit Gibbs distributions, with the renormalisation group for hierarchical models as its worked example.

sources.title: A non-Gaussian renormalization group fixed point for hierarchical scalar lattice field theories
sources.author: H. Koch and P. Wittwer
sources.description: A computer-assisted proof of a nontrivial fixed point of the hierarchical renormalisation map for scalar lattice fields, with no small parameter and no epsilon expansion.

sources.title: On the renormalization group transformation for scalar hierarchical models
sources.author: H. Koch and P. Wittwer
sources.description: The functional-analytic framework for the hierarchical renormalisation map on scalar models: the space of interactions, the map, and the estimates the fixed-point proof rests on.

sources.title: A nontrivial renormalization group fixed point for the Dyson-Baker hierarchical model
sources.author: H. Koch and P. Wittwer
sources.description: The same programme for the hierarchical model built on the Baker map, where the block structure comes from a piecewise linear expanding map of the interval.

sources.title: A complete renormalization group trajectory between two fixed points
sources.author: A. Abdesselam
sources.description: A rigorous nonperturbative construction of a massless trajectory of Wilson's exact renormalisation group joining the ultraviolet Gaussian fixed point to the nontrivial infrared fixed point, for a three-dimensional model with modified propagator.

sources.title: Renormalization group trajectories between two fixed points
sources.author: A. Abdesselam
sources.edition: Proc. XVI Int. Congr. Math. Phys. (Prague), 2010
sources.description: A six-page account of the construction of complete trajectories between fixed points: a fixed point argument in a Banach space of sequences obtained by perturbing a nonlinear one-dimensional iteration, without the hierarchical approximation.

sources.title: Towards three-dimensional conformal probability
sources.author: A. Abdesselam
sources.description: The ultrametric and p-adic counterparts of the hierarchical model, and the renormalisation group on them, as a route to a three-dimensional conformal field theory.

sources.title: Sharp hierarchical upper bounds on the critical two-point function for long-range percolation on Z^d
sources.author: T. Hutchcroft
sources.description: Hierarchical upper bounds, transported to the Euclidean lattice, on the critical two-point function of long-range percolation.

sources.title: Critical cluster volumes in hierarchical percolation
sources.author: T. Hutchcroft
sources.description: The volume of the critical cluster in hierarchical long-range percolation, and the exponent that governs its tail.

sources.title: Studium des Phasenuebergangs zweiter Art in Dysons asymptotischen hierarchischen Modellen
sources.author: P. M. Bleher
sources.description: A short announcement of the second-order phase transition in Dyson's asymptotically hierarchical models, preceding the detailed papers with Sinai.

sources.title: Construction of non-Gaussian self-similar random fields with hierarchical structure
sources.author: P. M. Bleher
sources.description: A construction of self-similar random fields with hierarchical structure, that is, of block-spin laws invariant under the renormalisation step.

sources.title: A theorem on large deviations in the neighbourhood of phi-fourth hierarchical models
sources.author: P. M. Bleher
sources.description: Large deviations for the hierarchical model with a phi-fourth single-spin distribution, the tool on which the low-temperature limit theorems rest.

sources.title: Limit theorems for multicomponent hierarchical models
sources.author: P. M. Bleher
sources.edition: Probability theory and mathematical statistics, Proc. 4th Vilnius Conf. (1985), Vol. 1, 211-229
sources.description: Limit theorems for the block sums of multicomponent hierarchical models: the vector case in which the limits need not be Gaussian.

sources.title: The large-scale limit of Dyson's hierarchical vector valued model at low temperatures. The non-Gaussian case
sources.author: P. M. Bleher and P. Major
sources.edition: Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Phys. Théor. 49 (1988), 7-85 and 87-143
sources.description: Two-part paper on the large-scale limit of the low-temperature vector-valued hierarchical model in the non-Gaussian case: a limit theorem for the average spin, and a description of the limiting field.

sources.title: Renormalization of Dyson's vector-valued hierarchical model at low temperatures
sources.author: P. M. Bleher and P. Major
sources.edition: Probability theory and mathematical statistics, Proc. 5th Vilnius Conf. (1989), Vol. I, 141-151
sources.description: A conference account of the low-temperature renormalisation of the vector-valued hierarchical model.

sources.title: Borel summability of the perturbation series in a hierarchical lambda (nabla phi)^4 model
sources.author: K. Gawedzki, A. Kupiainen and B. Tirozzi
sources.description: Borel summability of the perturbation series for a hierarchical gradient model: the technique with which the large-field region is brought under control.

sources.title: Triviality of phi-fourth in four dimensions and all that in a hierarchy model approximation
sources.author: K. Gawedzki and A. Kupiainen
sources.description: The hierarchy-model approximation used to discuss triviality of phi-fourth in four dimensions; cited by Koch and Wittwer as the analyticity technique their method improves on.

sources.title: Computing bounds on critical indices
sources.author: H. Koch and P. Wittwer
sources.edition: Nonlinear evolution and chaotic phenomena, Proc. NATO ASI (Noto, 1987), NATO ASI Ser. B 176, 269-277
sources.description: An outline of a computer-assisted proof giving rigorous bounds on the free-energy exponent, universal across a one-parameter family of hierarchical systems in three dimensions.

sources.title: The description of a random field by means of conditional probabilities and conditions of its regularity
sources.author: R. L. Dobrushin
sources.edition: Teor. Veroyatn. Primen. 13 (1968), 201-229; English translation: Theory Probab. Appl. 13, 197-224
sources.description: A random field described by its system of conditional probabilities, with a regularity condition under which the description determines the field: the origin of the formulation of a Gibbs measure by its conditional laws.

sources.title: Observables at infinity and states with short range correlations in statistical mechanics
sources.author: O. E. Lanford III and D. Ruelle
sources.description: States of an infinite system characterised by their conditional expectations given the configuration outside a finite region, with the equivalence between short-range correlations and the absence of dependence on observables at infinity.

sources.title: Gibbs Measures and Phase Transitions
sources.author: H.-O. Georgii
sources.edition: 2nd extended edition, De Gruyter Studies in Mathematics 9, de Gruyter, Berlin, 2011
sources.description: The general theory of Gibbs measures on lattice spin systems: specifications, the DLR characterisation, compactness of the set of Gibbs measures, and the passage from finite-volume measures, with phase transitions treated through the convex structure.

sources.title: Correlation inequalities on some partially ordered sets
sources.author: C. M. Fortuin, P. W. Kasteleyn and J. Ginibre
sources.description: Positive correlation of increasing functions for measures satisfying a positive lattice condition, covering ferromagnetic Ising and Potts models and percolation: the FKG inequality.

sources.title: Concavity of magnetization of an Ising ferromagnet in a positive external field
sources.author: R. B. Griffiths, C. A. Hurst and S. Sherman
sources.description: The magnetisation of a ferromagnetic Ising model is concave in a nonnegative external field, equivalently the third cumulant of any sum of spins is nonpositive: the GHS inequality. No zbMATH record was found for this work; it is cited by its published details.
